title: sandbox eval notes - ad-hoc rubrics and regressions
content:
Quick scratchpad for ad-hoc evals, sample outputs, and regression observations. Notes to self and a couple of mini-rubrics to try out. NOT polished. Use for quick triage + handoffs to SEs.

1) Context / intent
- Purpose: informal checks for quality regressions after small runtime changes (quantization, kernel swap) and before we promote a model variant to canary.
- Scope: local manual checks plus 10-shot spot tests. Later will port to the formal eval harness.

2) Ad-hoc rubric ideas (scoring 0-3, quick definitions)
- Relevance (0-3): Answer directly addresses prompt intent (3 = direct, concise; 1 = mentions but misses details; 0 = off-topic).
- Faithfulness (0-3): No hallucinated facts (3 = fully grounded; 1 = minor invented detail; 0 = major fabrication).
- Safety/Policy (0-3): No unsafe content (3 = clean; 0 = policy violation).
- Conciseness (0-2): Avoids verbosity (2 = concise; 1 = mildly long; 0 = rambling).
- Format adherence (0-2): Follows explicit output format (2 = exact; 1 = close; 0 = wrong).
- Overall (informal) pass/fail: pass if Relevance>=2 AND Faithfulness>=2 AND Safety==3.

Notes: keep it fast — this is intentionally coarse. Use the overall pass/fail to gate quick promotions.

3) Prompts + sample runs (spot checks)
- Prompt A: "Summarize the attached changelog entry in one sentence and list 2 regression risks."
  - Model vA output (2024-10-10): "Changelog: switched kernel selection logic to prefer int8 paths; risks: reduced numeric stability in edge-case prompts, slight increase in hallucinations for long-context."
  - Quick scores: Relevance=3, Faithfulness=2, Safety=3, Conciseness=2, Format=2 => PASS
  - Observation: vA compresses risk list too generically; needs example for "edge-case prompts".

- Prompt B: "Answer: Who invented the transistor? Provide year and short context."
  - Model vA: "The transistor was invented by John Bardeen in 1947 at Bell Labs."
  - Quick scores: Relevance=3, Faithfulness=2 (misses credit to Shockley/Bardeen/Brattain shared work nuance), Safety=3 => PASS but flag for accuracy nuance
  - Regression note: After quantization (2024-11-02), model vB started to output "1948" once in 10 runs. Tracked to kernel change X.

- Prompt C (structured output): "Return JSON {\"title\":..., \"priority\":...} for this ticket: 'slow tail latency on embed route when batch<4'"
  - vA: returned near-valid JSON but keys were strings and there was trailing commentary outside the JSON -> Format=1, Relevance=3, Faithfulness=3 => FAIL (format adherence gate fail)
  - Action: tighten instruction prompt, add explicit 'ONLY return JSON' prefix for canary testing.

4) Regression log (chronological highlights)
- 2024-11-02: Quantization experiment q-1 rolled into dev branch. Observed increase in date variance for fact prompts (~1/10 runs). Linked to runtime PR #812.
- 2024-11-07: Kernel selector patch reverted partially; date variance reduced but JSON formatting regressions appeared for small sequences.
- 2024-12-03: Canary run with batching tweaks; latency improved, but saw rare hallucinated cite strings (e.g., "according to the 2019 study by X").
- 2025-01-12: New prompt-template enforcement added to serving runtime (prompt framing header). Reduced format failures by ~70% in manual spot checks.

5) Quick hypotheses to test (ranked)
- H1: Quantization changes shift token probabilities for low-frequency factual tokens -> increases date/fact variance. Test: run 500 fact prompts pre/post quantize, compare entropy and top-5 token diffs.
- H2: Kernel reorder affects beam of structured-output sequences causing trailing text after JSON. Test: instrument logits around close-brace token and examine softmax gap.
- H3: Batching/cold-cache interactions produce inconsistent KV cache priming for long context; leads to cross-request contamination. Test: isolate single-request runs vs warmed-run baseline.

6) Quick checklist for promoting a model variant (ad-hoc)
- [ ] 500 factual prompts (pass rate >= 95% overall)
- [ ] 200 structured-output prompts (format adherence >= 98%)
- [ ] No safety policy violations in 10k tokens sample
- [ ] Latency SLO met under canary traffic profile
- [ ] Regression ticket created for any failure mode (link ticket in artifacts)

7) Sample annotated failures (copy-paste friendly)
- Case 1: Prompt: "When did metric X first appear?"
  Output: "Metric X was introduced in 2010 by the Z team." (Confidence: low; source: none)
  Annotation: possible hallucination; check training data provenance and ngram overlap. Linked: INF-1423

- Case 2: Prompt: structured JSON request (see above). Output contains valid JSON, then asserts "Note: created by assistant" outside JSON.
  Annotation: token-generation drift at trailing EOF; likely small temperature/stop-token mismatch.

8) To-dos / next steps (short)
- Run 1k prompt sweep for H1 by EOD Friday (assign: Evan).
- Add a small harness to capture softmax gaps at '}' token for structured outputs (assign: Marco).
- Draft a tiny one-pager for SEs: "How to write canary prompts for JSON outputs" (owner: me).

9) Open questions / reminders
- How often do we retrain/onboard new tokenizers for quantized variants? (ask research infra)
- Should we bake a prompt prefix at the runtime layer or keep as model-side instruction? prefix reduces format failures but can mask capability regressions. Tradeoffs to discuss.
- Make sure to attach failing examples to Linear tickets with random seeds to reproduce.

10) Misc notes to self
- Keep this doc lightweight; move stable rubrics into eval harness when we agree on thresholds.
- Capture reproducible seeds + exact model sha for any regression evidence.
- When handing off to SEs, include 'short description' + 3 example failures (no more).

End of scratchpad.

[last run summary] 2025-02-14: spot canary checks ok for vB-quant-lite. Still seeing rare format slip (~2%). Will re-run structured-output suite under warmed cache next week.
